'''Zhang Lina''' ({{lang-zh|first=s|s=张俐娜|p=Zhāng Lìnà}}; 14 August 1940 – 17 October 2020) was a Chinese physical chemist specializing in polymer science. She focused on high-performance mechanisms of biomass based materials such as soy protein, alginate and cellulose; all are a part of [[green chemistry]]. She was a dedicated educator, training 118 postgraduate and doctoral students.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Cai |first=Jie |last2=Huang |first2=Jin |date=2021 |title=Dedicate to commemorate of Prof. Lina Zhang |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/app.51608 |journal=Journal of Applied Polymer Science |language=en |volume=138 |issue=48 |article-number=51608 |doi=10.1002/app.51608 |issn=1097-4628}}</ref>  Zhang was elected as an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], becoming the first woman from Wuhan University to receive this honor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://en.whu.edu.cn/info/1050/1470.htm|title=Wuhan University|website=en.whu.edu.cn|access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
Zhang Lina graduated from [[Wuhan University]] in 1963<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.whu.edu.cn/info/1183/3171.htm|title=张俐娜-武汉大学|website=www.whu.edu.cn|access-date=2016-03-05|archive-date=12 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412181133/http://www.whu.edu.cn/info/1183/3171.htm}}</ref><ref name="people">{{cite web|last1=Qu|first1=Jiancheng|title=武汉大学第一位女院士 张俐娜演绎"神话般故事"|url=http://edu.people.com.cn/n/2014/0319/c1053-24673368.html|website=Renmin Wang|access-date=5 March 2016}}</ref> and later became a distinguished professor at the School of Chemistry and Molecular Sciences of [[Wuhan University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://en.whu.edu.cn/info/1073/1566.htm|title=Wuhan University|website=en.whu.edu.cn|access-date=2020-04-07|archive-date=7 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200307012351/https://en.whu.edu.cn/info/1073/1566.htm}}</ref> Zhang studied in Japan through a Japan Society for the Promotion of Science scholarship at Osaka University in 1984–1986. There she started work on green chemistry by studying polysaccharide solutions.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=The cellulose specialist |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/careers/the-cellulose-specialist/1017336.article |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Chemistry World |language=en}}</ref>

Zhang founded the Natural Polymer and Polymer Physics Research Group at Wuhan University in 1993. Zhang's research focused on fundamental and applied research of biomass resources and natural macromolecular material science.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Santiago Cintrón |first=Michael |date=2011-08-01 |title=Professor Lina Zhang wins the 2011 Anselme Payen award of the Division of Cellulose and Renewable Materials |journal=Cellulose |language=en |volume=18 |issue=4 |pages=857–858 |doi=10.1007/s10570-011-9553-8 |issn=1572-882X}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> She solved the problem of the poorest soluble biomass macromolecule, cellulose.<ref name=":3" /> [[Cellulose]] is a rich renewable resource from plants, but the use of traditional manufacturing technology which used CS<sub>2</sub>/NaOH harms sustainable development of the environment. In 2000, sponsored by the Natural Science Foundation of China,<ref name=":4" /> Zhang broke through the traditional method of polymer dissolution by heating and successfully dissolved [[cellulose]] and [[chitin]] using an [[Sodium hydroxide|NaOH]]/[[urea]] solution at low temperature.<ref name="Wuhan University">{{Cite web|url=https://en.whu.edu.cn/info/1081/2643.htm|title=Wuhan University|website=en.whu.edu.cn|access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref> Zhang's technology reduces the generation of white pollution, and the materials generated using Zhang's technology can be completely degraded within a month. This technology makes the recycling of biomass waste possible and renewable resources can be better utilized.<ref name="Wuhan University" /> Zhang pioneered new technology for low-temperature dissolution of polymers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://yswk.las.ac.cn/qiantai/Shouye_zhanshi.action?id=2011B03#|title=中国科学院院士文库|website=yswk.las.ac.cn|access-date=2020-03-01}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Throughout her career, Zhang published over 530 papers in international journals and was granted nearly 100 patents. Her work is highly influential in the field of "[[Self-healing hydrogels]]" and "Regenerated cellulose," with her top-cited paper, Rapid dissolution of cellulose in LiOH/urea and NaOH/urea aqueous solutions, receiving over 1,200 citations.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=2026 Lina Zhang: Chemistry Researcher – H-Index, Publications & Awards |url=https://research.com/u/lina-zhang |access-date=2026-03-09 |website=Research.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Research and Innovation ==
Zhang's most significant contribution was the development of a "green" method to dissolve cellulose. Unlike traditional methods that use high heat and toxic chemicals (the [[Viscose process]]), Zhang discovered that a pre-cooled aqueous solution of [[LiOH]]/urea or NaOH/urea could rapidly dissolve cellulose at low temperatures (around -12&nbsp;°C).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cai |first=Jie |last2=Zhang |first2=Lina |date=2005-06-24 |title=Rapid Dissolution of Cellulose in LiOH/Urea and NaOH/Urea Aqueous Solutions |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mabi.200400222 |journal=Macromolecular Bioscience |language=en |volume=5 |issue=6 |pages=539–548 |doi=10.1002/mabi.200400222 |issn=1616-5195|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This discovery is considered a milestone in polymer science because it allows for the creation of biodegradable films and fibers without environmental pollution.<ref name=":5" />

== Achievements ==
Zhang has published 530 papers, authored 16 books, and been granted nearly 100 domestic and international patents.<ref name=":6">{{cite web|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/careers/the-cellulose-specialist/1017336.article|title=The cellulose specialist|last=Chapman |first=Kit |date=2016-10-03 |website=Chemistry World|access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref>

In 2006, Zhang wrote book ''Natural polymer modified materials and applications.''<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://yswk.las.ac.cn/search/search_zylxlistnew.action?pageId=1586233822005&searchmod=init&id=1&bh=2011B03&lx=cjzz|title=中国科学院院士文库|website=yswk.las.ac.cn|access-date=2020-04-07}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In 2007, Zhang wrote book ''Natural Polymer Science and Materials.''<ref name=":2" />

In 2011, Zhang wrote book ''Environmentally friendly materials based on biomass.''<ref name=":2" />

In 2015, Zhang wrote book ''Cellulose Science and Materials.''<ref name=":2" />

In 2011, she became the first Chinese scientist to receive the [[Anselme Payen Award]], the highest international honor in the field of cellulose and renewable materials, awarded by the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS). The award included a bronze medal and a $3,000 honorarium.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cell.sites.acs.org/anselmepayenaward.htm|title=Anselme Payen Award|website=Cellulose and Renewable Materials Division|access-date=2016-03-05|archive-date=1 March 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110301022916/http://cell.sites.acs.org/anselmepayenaward.htm}}</ref><ref name=":6" />

In 2011, she was elected as an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], becoming the first woman from Wuhan University to receive this honor.<ref name=":0" />

Zhang served on the editorial boards of ''Cellulose, the Journal of Biobased Materials and Bioenergy, and Acta Polymerica Sinica.''<ref name=":1" />
